orig=[list(map(int,line.split())) for line in s.splitlines()]
out=[row[:] for row in orig]
# Erase top diagrams (their original background is 4).
for r in range(2,7):
    for c in range(9,16): out[r][c]=4
for r in range(1,5):
    for c in range(19,23): out[r][c]=4
# Render a color-specific mask: target-color pixels become panel side color;
# all other cells in that color's bbox become the panel's base color.
def paste_mask(src, color, bbox, panel_top, panel_bottom, panel_side, panel_base):
    r0,r1,c0,c1=bbox
    cells=[(r,c) for r in range(r0,r1+1) for c in range(c0,c1+1) if src[r][c]==color]
    rr0=min(r for r,c in cells); rr1=max(r for r,c in cells)
    cc0=min(c for r,c in cells); cc1=max(c for r,c in cells)
    h=rr1-rr0+1
    dy=panel_bottom-h+1
    # Keep original x position and align bottom within the matching panel.
    for r in range(rr0,rr1+1):
        for c in range(cc0,cc1+1):
            out[dy+(r-rr0)][c] = panel_side if src[r][c]==color else panel_base
# 7-patterns from both upper tiles -> rows 13..20, base 7 / side 3
paste_mask(orig,7,(2,6,9,15),13,20,3,7)
paste_mask(orig,7,(1,4,19,22),13,20,3,7)
# 3-patterns from both upper tiles -> rows 22..27, base 3 / side 9
paste_mask(orig,3,(2,6,9,15),22,27,9,3)
paste_mask(orig,3,(1,4,19,22),22,27,9,3)
